stories.title: Former airline pilot in South Korea gets life for murder, plot to kill 5 others
stories.summary: A former South Korean airline pilot was sentenced to life imprisonment for murdering one colleague and plotting to kill five others. He meticulously planned attacks over seven months, including stalking victims, using tracking devices, and accessing flight schedules illegally. The court rejected his claims of unfair treatment, citing lack of remorse and risk of re-offending, ordering permanent isolation and electronic monitoring for 30 years. A 49-year-old former airline pilot in South Korea who plotted to kill six former colleagues and fatally stabbed one of them was sentenced to life in prison on Aug 21. The Busan District Court convicted Kim Dong-hwan of murder, attempted murder, preparing to commit murder, trespassing and violating information network laws. The court also ordered him to wear an electronic tracking device for 30 years. Kim was accused of fatally stabbing a former airline captain at an apartment in Busanjin-gu, Busan, on March 17. A day earlier, he attempted to kill another former colleague, also an airline captain, at a residence in Goyang, Gyeonggi Province, prosecutors said. He had planned to kill four other people connected to his former employer. Prosecutors said Kim had prepared for the attacks for more than seven months from August 2025, following his targets, attaching tracking devices to vehicles and surveying their homes and daily routines. He also allegedly used a former colleague’s account to access the airline’s internal flight schedule system 17 times to check the victims’ schedules. The court said the crimes were carefully planned and brutal, and it rejected Kim’s claim that he had been driven to the attacks after being unfairly treated by former colleagues with backgrounds at the Korea Air Force Academy.

stories.title: Plane with eight people on board crashes in Alaska — Associated Press
stories.summary: NEW YORK, August 21. A plane with eight people on board has crashed in the west of Alaska, Associated Press reported citing the National Transportation Safety Board. The report says that the plane, with two pilots and six passengers, took off from Anchorage and crashed somewhere around Cape Newnham. A search and rescue effort is under way. The fate of those on board is currently unknown.
